stem: When a person is vaccinated, their own immune system is stimulated to produce antibodies against a weakened/inactivated pathogen, providing long-lasting protection. This type of immunity, generated by the body's own response, is called:
explanation: Active immunity develops when the body's own immune system produces antibodies (via infection or vaccination), giving durable, long-term protection — unlike passive immunity, where ready-made antibodies are directly transferred into the body (e.g., from mother to infant via breast milk, or via an antibody injection), giving only temporary protection.
